record.tranche_reason: The paper gives a theoretical reinterpretation of SAE features as thematic components rather than monosemantic, steerable mechanisms. This bears on the claim about SAE features as canonical units, but it does not empirically test superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The reported topic-coherence, diversity, and relevance scores evaluate topic-model performance, not superposition, feature geometry, or feature completeness and stability; they are not recorded as rows. Results cited from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The paper derives the L1 SAE objective as MAP inference under an assumed continuous topic model. It then uses SAEs as a topic-modelling tool on document and image embeddings, reporting only topic coherence, diversity and relevance against topic-model baselines. The derivation holds only if the assumed generative model is true, and the paper never tests that model on real representations. It never measures completeness, stability or canonicality of SAE features, and the SAEs are trained on output embeddings (Granite-R2, SigLIP), not on model internals. Its claim that features are 'thematic components rather than steerable directions' is an interpretive argument, not a result on any version. The reader's T5/tests guess is not supported.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors report SAE-TM beats neural topic-model baselines on coherence (intruder detection and rating) across five text and three image datasets, with diversity second-best on text and weaker on images. The steering claim is argued from the derivation, not tested.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops a continuous topic-model derivation and evaluates SAEs as topic models; it does not reproduce the original toy-network superposition experiments or their geometry measurements.

fits_no_version.finding: Under assumptions A1–A3, the L1-penalty SAE objective equals MAP inference in an LDA-like continuous topic model. Fixed-sparsity SAEs correspond to a hard-support approximation. The authors read SAE features as thematic components, not monosemantic steerable mechanisms.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features on embedding spaces are best interpreted as topic atoms (mixture components of themes) rather than mechanistic, steerable units.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The argument about feature interpretation depends on theoretical assumptions; the paper does not empirically test canonicality, feature stability, or superposition geometry.
record.rows_left_out: Topic-model benchmark results in Tables 2–9 are omitted because they measure topic quality and comparison with topic-model baselines, not the claim versions about superposition or canonical SAE units.

untested.parts: All: no toy networks, geometry or sparsity transition.
All: no capacity or polysemanticity analysis.
All: SAEs are fit to output embedding datasets, not LLM internal activations; no feature-spreading measure.
Completeness, stability across seeds or sizes, and canonicality of SAE features are not measured; the thematic-component reading is argued theoretically only.
The derivation assumes 1-D concentrated topic directions (A2) but does not test it.

record.verdict_notes: Topic-quality tables (2–9) are the authors' own method compared against baselines, so they are rightly left out as rows. No steering experiments are run despite the steerability claim.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-network overlap geometry, near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
The paper applies SAEs to embedding datasets, not LLM internal activations, and does not test feature distribution across neurons or recovery of LLM activation features.
The theoretical reinterpretation bears on whether SAE features are monosemantic units, but the paper does not test their completeness, stability, or canonicality.
The model assumes concentrated topic directions for its SAE derivation; it does not test whether actual features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: L1-penalty SAE objective under the continuous topic model (CTM)
rows.operation_detail: Theoretically derive the SAE objective as a MAP estimator under the CTM and interpret the resulting features.

conditions.value: A1–A3: high-activity, small-contribution limit; concentrated topic directions; independence across topics

rows.measure: Theoretical relationship between the SAE objective and CTM feature interpretation
rows.value: Under the stated assumptions, the L1-penalty SAE objective is a MAP estimator under the CTM; the authors characterize SAE features as thematic components rather than monosemantic, steerable mechanisms.
rows.note: This is a theoretical result and interpretive argument, not an empirical test of feature completeness, stability, or canonicality.
rows.check: This row records a theoretical derivation conditional on assumptions A1–A3 (κ=1, αk=1), not a measured result. It does not measure whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical units of a model's representation, so it cannot bear on V5. Its state 'partial' has no baseline or value to rest on. Move it to fits_no_version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
